questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the real, well-documented reason most CMDB implementations fail?
options: Identification Rules always stop working after a few months
The ServiceNow platform cannot technically sustain good data quality past launch
Standing up technical configuration (Discovery, Identification/Reconciliation rules) without ongoing accountable ownership to keep it accurate over time
Discovery is incapable of running more than once
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this is almost never a technical platform limitation -- it's a governance gap.

questions.q: What is a Business/Technical Service Owner accountable for?
options: Whether the service's representation in the CMDB -- its CIs, mapping, and relationships -- stays accurate as the service changes
Writing Identification Rules for every CI class
Approving Stripe subscription changes for the platform
Running Discovery schedules for the entire CMDB
questions.explain: This role tracks a specific service's CMDB accuracy over time, not the whole CMDB's technical configuration.

questions.q: How is a CI-class data owner's accountability scoped, compared to a Service Owner's?
options: A CI-class data owner is accountable for that class's data quality across the whole CMDB, regardless of which service any individual CI supports
CI-class data owners and Service Owners have identical scopes
CI-class data owners are only responsible for duplicate detection, nothing else
A CI-class data owner only cares about CIs tied to one specific business service
questions.explain: The person who owns cmdb_ci_server data quality cares about every server CI platform-wide, not just ones tied to a single application.

questions.q: Why does a defined review cadence matter, beyond just naming an owner?
options: A review cadence replaces the need for a named owner entirely
Ownership without a schedule tends to collapse into 'I'll get to it eventually,' so a recurring cadence is what actually closes the loop
ServiceNow automatically enforces review cadences with no human involvement
Cadence only matters for the duplicate rate score, not the others
questions.explain: A score plus a named owner plus a scheduled review is what the lesson identifies as the mechanism that keeps data accurate over time.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about the relationship between technical configuration and governance?
options: Governance can fully replace the need for Discovery and Identification/Reconciliation rules
Governance and technical configuration address the exact same problem
Technical configuration is necessary but not sufficient -- it has no memory or accountability on its own and will let a correct CMDB decay unwatched
Technical configuration alone is sufficient if it was built correctly on day one
questions.explain: Both are required -- technical rules produce accurate data, but governance is what gives them a reason to stay correct past the initial build.
